prompts.label: Node.js Hello World
prompts.text:
I'm new to Node.js. Create a minimal project.

- package.json with name and type module (ESM) OR CommonJS — pick one and explain
- index.js that logs Hello from Node
- Commands: npm init, node index.js

Mention Node LTS version briefly.

prompts.label: DOM click counter
prompts.text:
Build a beginner DOM exercise: click counter.

- index.html with a button and a span showing count starting at 0
- script.js: click increments count, second button resets to 0
- Link script with defer
- No frameworks

Explain querySelector, addEventListener, and textContent.

prompts.label: fetch() load JSON
prompts.text:
Create a small page that loads JSON with fetch.

- Fetch https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1
- Show name and email in the HTML after load
- Show a loading message and an error message if fetch fails
- Use async/await

Provide index.html and script.js.

prompts.label: Express Hello server
prompts.text:
Create the smallest Express server for a beginner.

- server.js: GET / returns Hello from Express
- package.json with express dependency and start script
- Steps: npm install, npm start, test in browser
- Add GET /api/time returning current ISO time as JSON

Use CommonJS or ESM consistently and say which you chose.

prompts.label: React component skeleton
prompts.text:
I'm starting with React. Scaffold a minimal app with Vite (npm create vite@latest).

- One App component showing a title and a button that increments a counter (useState)
- Explain folder structure after create
- List commands to install and run dev server

Keep one file change at a time if possible; focus on JSX and props concept in 2–3 sentences.

prompts.label: Form validation (vanilla)
prompts.text:
Build a sign-up form with client-side validation (no backend).

- Fields: username (min 3 chars), email, password (min 8 chars), confirm password
- On submit: prevent default, show inline error messages
- Clear errors when user fixes input
- Vanilla JS only

Provide HTML, CSS, and JS.

prompts.label: Todo list (vanilla JS)
prompts.text:
Create a simple todo list app for learning JavaScript.

- Input + Add button creates a list item
- Each item: checkbox (complete), delete button
- Completed items show strikethrough
- Store todos in an array in memory (localStorage optional bonus)

Full HTML/CSS/JS with short comments.

prompts.label: ES modules import/export
prompts.text:
Teach ES modules with a tiny example.

- math.js exports add and multiply functions
- main.js imports them and logs results
- index.html loads main.js as type="module"
- Explain named vs default export in one paragraph

Show exact file tree and how to run with a static server (npx serve or Live Server).

prompts.label: async/await delay demo
prompts.text:
Explain async/await with a beginner demo (Node or browser).

- Function fetchUser() that waits 1 second then returns { id: 1, name: 'Ada' }
- Main async function prints Loading..., then user, using try/catch
- Compare briefly with .then() chains

Provide runnable code and expected console output.

prompts.label: package.json npm scripts
prompts.text:
Explain package.json scripts for a beginner JS project.

- Example package.json with scripts: start, dev (nodemon or vite), test (placeholder echo)
- What npm run start does vs npx
- devDependencies vs dependencies with one example each
- .gitignore for node_modules

Use a realistic but minimal project name.

prompts.label: Fix closures inside loops
prompts.text:
I'm running async callbacks in a loop and every item logs the wrong index/value.
Explain the historical var closure pitfall and the modern fix with let or with an IIFE pattern.
Give a clean for...of + await example for sequential calls.
Note when Promise.all with map is appropriate instead.
End with a 3-item checklist to spot similar bugs in event listeners.

prompts.label: Sort arrays without mutating surprises
prompts.text:
Teach me array sort pitfalls in JavaScript for interview prep level beginners.
Show how sort() mutates in place and how to copy with slice or spread first.
Provide a numeric comparator for numbers and a localeCompare example for names.
Explain stable vs unstable sort at a high level.
Warn about comparing objects without a comparator.

prompts.label: AbortController for cancellable fetch
prompts.text:
I want a fetch that can be aborted when the user navigates away or clicks Cancel.
Walk through AbortController + signal wiring on fetch.
Demonstrate a timeout pattern using AbortSignal.timeout if available, with a fallback.
Show how to catch AbortError separately from network errors.
Keep the example under one small module with comments.

prompts.label: URL and URLSearchParams parsing
prompts.text:
Compare hand-rolling query strings vs using URL and URLSearchParams.
Build a tiny helper that reads current page query params in the browser and safely encodes a new link.
Explain why decodeURIComponent can be dangerous if misused.
Touch on base URL resolution with new URL(relative, base).
Give one Node.js example reading process.argv vs import.meta.url context briefly.

prompts.label: Intl for dates and numbers
prompts.text:
Show beginners how Intl.NumberFormat and Intl.DateTimeFormat improve presentation.
Examples: currency in EUR, compact notation for large dashboard counts, short weekday in a locale.
Note timezone pitfalls: what the API can and cannot infer.
Compare to manual string concatenation anti-patterns.
Include feature detection thoughts for older browsers at a high level.

prompts.label: Custom Error subclasses
prompts.text:
I throw plain strings sometimes and want to improve.
Demonstrate class ValidationError extends Error with a code field and correct prototype chain.
Explain why instanceof checks matter in catch blocks.
Show capturing cause in modern engines when wrapping errors.
Give a pattern for mapping errors to HTTP statuses without frameworks.

prompts.label: WeakMap for private memoization idea
prompts.text:
At a beginner-friendly depth, explain Map vs WeakMap and why keys must be objects.
Sketch a tiny memoizeByObject(fn) using WeakMap for per-object caches that don't leak memory.
Contrast with a global Map keyed by strings.
Call out when this pattern is overkill.
No heavy algorithm analysis—just intuition and a 15-line demo.

prompts.label: structuredClone for deep copies
prompts.text:
Teach structuredClone as a modern alternative to JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(obj)).
List what types clone well and what fails (functions, symbols, DOM nodes).
Compare shallow copy with spread for nested objects.
Mention Same-Transferable considerations only lightly.
Provide two micro-examples: nested plain object and Date preservation.

prompts.label: Event loop mental model cartoon
prompts.text:
Help me predict console order for setTimeout, Promise.then, and sync code.
Explain the call stack, task queue, and microtask queue in plain language.
Give a short puzzle and solution walkthrough.
Relate why await can reorder perceived execution.
Finish with debugging advice using breakpoints vs console.log spacing.

prompts.label: Module import maps in the browser
prompts.text:
I see import maps mentioned for using npm packages directly in browsers without bundlers.
Outline the idea, trade-offs, and a minimal index.html snippet with script type importmap.
Explain when beginners should still prefer Vite instead.
Note CORS considerations for module scripts.
List one security footgun about remote module URLs.

prompts.label: Proxy and Reflect basics
prompts.text:
I want to validate object writes without a heavy library.
Explain Proxy traps get/set and when Reflect helps keep default behavior.
Build a tiny createValidatedUser() that rejects negative age assignments.
Contrast Proxy cost and debugging difficulty for beginners.
List two real-world cases (observability, ORM) vs when plain objects suffice.

prompts.label: Set and Map when to use them
prompts.text:
Teach Set vs array uniqueness and Map vs plain object keys.
Show deduping tags with Set, counting occurrences with Map.
Explain why object keys are always strings and when Map wins.
Provide a beginner exercise: unique visitors from a click log array.
End with a checklist for picking Set/Map/Record in small apps.

prompts.label: RegExp patterns for logs
prompts.text:
Walk through constructing a RegExp to extract ISO dates and status codes from log lines.
Explain flags i, m, g and capturing groups with named groups if supported.
Show test() vs exec() vs matchAll() briefly.
Warn about catastrophic backtracking at a headline level.
Give three test strings and expected matches as a mini quiz.

prompts.label: debounce and throttle utilities
prompts.text:
Explain debounce vs throttle with a search box and a scroll listener example.
Implement both in plain JS without lodash, with cancel on unmount notes for SPAs.
Describe leading vs trailing edge behavior in plain language.
Show how to test timing with fake timers conceptually (Vitest optional).
Finish with when neither is needed (small lists).

prompts.label: localStorage persistence pattern
prompts.text:
Build a theme preference saved to localStorage with try/catch for private mode.
Explain quota limits, synchronous API pitfalls, and JSON.stringify gotchas (Date, undefined).
Show namespacing keys with a project prefix.
Contrast sessionStorage vs localStorage in one paragraph.
Add a security note: never store tokens unencrypted.

prompts.label: History API pushState
prompts.text:
Teach history.pushState and popstate for a fake tab switcher without a framework.
Update document title optionally and sync a nav highlight.
Explain why real apps still use routers.
Show how back button should restore prior tab state.
Provide index.html + script.js sketch and manual test steps.

prompts.label: Web Components custom element
prompts.text:
Introduce custom elements with a <hello-badge> showing a name attribute.
Use connectedCallback and attributeChangedCallback at beginner depth.
Explain shadow DOM boundary lightly (defer styling details to another prompt).
Compare Web Components vs React when to choose each.
List browser support and progressive enhancement idea.

prompts.label: Service Worker sketch offline
prompts.text:
Outline registering a service worker that caches a shell HTML for offline refresh.
Explain install/activate/fetch events in order without building a full PWA course.
Warn about cache busting and update prompts for users.
Note HTTPS requirement and localhost exception.
Give a minimal file tree and what to check in Application tab.

prompts.label: BroadcastChannel tab sync
prompts.text:
Show two tabs syncing a simple counter or logout event via BroadcastChannel.
Explain channel name collisions and closing channels on unload.
Contrast with localStorage storage event hack.
Mention when SharedWorker might appear in advanced reading.
Provide runnable HTML snippets for two windows.

prompts.label: crypto.randomUUID ids
prompts.text:
Replace Math.random ids with crypto.randomUUID() for client-side entities.
Explain collision probability at a friendly level.
Show fallback pattern if API missing in old browsers.
Discuss when server should still assign authoritative ids.
Add checklist: prefix ids in logs, don't trust client ids for auth.

prompts.label: PerformanceObserver metrics
prompts.text:
Introduce PerformanceObserver watching paint or LCP entries.
Log timings to console in a tiny static page.
Relate metrics to real UX improvements beginners can make (font, image size).
Mention privacy and sampling in production briefly.
List devtools Performance panel as validation step.

prompts.label: Vitest first unit test
prompts.text:
Scaffold Vitest on a small pure functions module.
Write tests for edge cases (empty array, negative number) with expect and describe.
Explain watch mode vs CI single run.
Compare to Jest migration mental model in two sentences.
End with package.json scripts and first npx vitest run commands.

prompts.label: ESLint flat config starter
prompts.text:
Migrate mentally from .eslintrc to flat config eslint.config.js.
Enable recommended rules for a browser + Node hybrid folder.
Show how to ignore dist/ and explain fix vs warn for learners.
Integrate one npm script lint.
Note @eslint/js and typescript-eslint pointer without full monorepo setup.

prompts.label: Iterator helpers fromEntries
prompts.text:
Explain Iterator.from, .map, .filter, .take helpers with a numbers pipeline example.
Contrast with array methods and lazy evaluation intuition.
Show converting back with Array.from or [...iter].
Mention engine support and polyfill caution.
Give a 5-line before/after readability comparison.

prompts.label: Object.groupBy reporting
prompts.text:
Given an array of { category, amount } rows, group totals with Object.groupBy.
Compare to manual reduce for readability.
Handle missing keys and empty groups gracefully.
Show printing a simple ASCII table to console.
Relate to SQL GROUP BY analogy for beginners.

prompts.label: Promise.allSettled batch jobs
prompts.text:
Fetch three endpoints with Promise.allSettled and summarize fulfilled vs rejected.
Explain why allSettled beats all when one failure should not cancel others.
Map results to a UI-friendly status list pattern.
Show typing results in TypeScript as optional bonus sentence.
End with retry strategy name-drop only.

prompts.label: Symbols for private-ish keys
prompts.text:
Teach Symbol as unique property keys and well-known symbols briefly (iterator).
Demonstrate hiding helper methods from JSON.stringify.
Explain symbols are not private in security sense.
Contrast with # private fields mention.
Provide a tiny class or object module example.

prompts.label: dynamic import code splitting
prompts.text:
Load a heavy chart module only when user clicks Show chart using dynamic import().
Show loading and error UI states around await import().
Explain Vite/Webpack splitting at high level.
Mention module federation as advanced scaling option for micro-frontends.
List devtools Network tab check for separate chunk.

prompts.label: Clipboard API copy button
prompts.text:
Build a Copy code button using navigator.clipboard.writeText with feature detection.
Handle permission errors and fallback execCommand note for older browsers.
Explain secure context HTTPS requirement.
Add user feedback toast pattern in words.
Include accessibility: button label and success announcement idea.

prompts.label: ResizeObserver responsive canvas
prompts.text:
Use ResizeObserver to resize a canvas or chart when its container changes.
Explain why window resize alone is insufficient in flex layouts.
Show cleanup disconnect in SPA teardown.
Warn about observation loops if modifying size in callback.
Give minimal HTML/CSS/JS demo structure.

prompts.label: IntersectionObserver lazy images
prompts.text:
Implement lazy-loading images with IntersectionObserver swapping data-src to src.
Explain rootMargin preloading threshold tuning.
Show unobserve after load to save work.
Contrast native loading=lazy attribute honestly.
Provide checklist for CLS: width/height attributes.

prompts.label: passive event listeners scroll
prompts.text:
Explain { passive: true } on touch/wheel listeners and scroll jank relationship.
Show adding a listener that cannot call preventDefault when passive.
Demonstrate feature detection for passive support.
Relate to Chrome console violations beginners see.
Give before/after advice for mobile menu scroll locking.

prompts.label: CSP and CORS primer
prompts.text:
Explain Content-Security-Policy default-src and script-src at beginner level with one policy example.
Contrast CORS: why browser blocks fetch to another origin and what Access-Control-Allow-Origin does.
Describe preflight OPTIONS mentally without full spec.
Warn that CORS is not auth.
List devtools Network error symptoms and who fixes server vs client.

prompts.label: Playwright first browser test
prompts.text:
Write the first Playwright test opening a local static page and asserting heading text.
Explain npx playwright install and headed vs headless.
Use role-based locators getByRole encouragement.
Show trace-on-failure config name-drop.
End with npm script test:e2e placeholder.

prompts.label: Optional chaining deep dive
prompts.text:
Teach ?. for nested API JSON and ?? for nullish defaults vs || pitfalls.
Show optional call obj?.method?.() and array?.[0].
Provide buggy examples using && chains and fix them.
Explain short-circuiting behavior in words.
Finish with style guide: don't chain 5 levels—normalize data instead.

prompts.label: Generators and yield sequences
prompts.text:
Introduce function* and yield with a simple ID generator or paginated fetch iterator sketch.
Explain how for...of consumes generators.
Contrast with async generators name-drop for streams.
Warn about forgetting to call .next() termination.
Give a 15-line teaching example only.

prompts.label: Array.from patterns
prompts.text:
Show Array.from on array-like (arguments, NodeList) and mapping indices in one pass.
Build range(1, n) helper for beginners.
Contrast spread [...nodeList] when map not needed.
Combine with Object.keys for enumerating records.
Add one pitfall: sparse arrays behavior.

prompts.label: JSON.parse reviver dates
prompts.text:
Demonstrate JSON.parse reviver turning date strings back into Date objects.
Explain toJSON on Date during stringify symmetry.
Warn about timezone assumptions.
Show safe parsing with try/catch and schema validation pointer (Zod).
Provide round-trip example object.

prompts.label: queueMicrotask ordering puzzle
prompts.text:
Explain queueMicrotask vs Promise.then vs setTimeout ordering with a short console puzzle.
Relate to mutation observer and render timing at high level.
Advise when to prefer microtasks for consistency fixes.
Warn against starving macrotasks.
Give solution walkthrough after puzzle.

prompts.label: Shadow DOM encapsulation
prompts.text:
Extend a custom element with attachShadow({ mode: 'open' }) and internal styles.
Explain style leakage prevention and ::part/::slotted teaser.
Show slot for light DOM projection.
Contrast open vs closed shadow roots for testing.
List one limitation for global design systems.
